definition: “Taking a motion off calendar” means canceling a hearing on a motion that has already been noticed. There are many circumstances in which attorneys may decide that a motion does not need to be heard. It can be a unilateral decision by one party, or it can be made after consulting with opposing counsel. Where a pleading has been marked off the calendar and there is no litigation-related activity thereafter, the court may decline to restore the case to the calendar and may regard it as abandoned. Related Terms:  Failure to appear is closely related to taking a motion off calendar.  The difference is parties need to notify the court before taking a motion off calendar. The way to notify the court varies.  A late “taking off calendar” means lawyers taking the motion off calendar at the last minute.  Judges can sanction lawyers for a late “taking off calendar”.
